input: research.json and topic-map.json. No page count or outline was given.
method: Start from the topic map's natural boundaries. Each boundary is a candidate page.
Split a candidate when its concepts need more than one Diataxis job (one page, one job).
Merge small neighbors that share one job and would not stand alone.
Order pages so every concept's dependsOn is taught on the same page or an earlier one. The entry reader is assumed to know none of the mapped concepts.
Anything the subject implies but the lab should not do goes in excluded, with a reason.

verdict.why: The subject holds several jobs (learn by doing, do a task, look up, understand why) and a dependency chain eight concepts deep, from addressing through isolation to decoy review. One page cannot give each concept a page before it that teaches its dependencies.

pages.title: Decide what your lab may watch, and why
pages.outcome: Can write a one-page scope for their lab: the devices and traffic they may observe, and the one failure they most want to catch.

pages.title: How your home network is wired
pages.outcome: Can draw their own network with addresses, subnet, and router, and say what the router does between inside and outside.

pages.title: Find what is listening on your machine
pages.outcome: Can list every listening service on one machine they own, and say for each one who can reach it and why it exists.

pages.title: Inventory every device you own and keep a baseline
pages.outcome: Can produce a dated device and listener baseline for their network and spot a change against it.

pages.title: What a firewall rule does, and why NAT is not one
pages.outcome: Can explain why their router blocks some inbound traffic, and name the cases (IPv6, port forwards) where it doesn't.

pages.title: Close silent exposure and test it from outside
pages.outcome: Can turn off UPnP, list existing port forwards, and prove a blocked path fails from both sides.

pages.title: Build the lab boundary
pages.outcome: Can put the lab behind a router they control and prove it cannot reach a trusted device.

pages.title: What a sensor can see, and where it has to sit
pages.outcome: Can say what a mirror port copies, where the sensor must sit to see lab traffic, and what metadata shows without content.

pages.title: Run Zeek and read your first day of logs
pages.outcome: Can run Zeek on a mirrored lab segment and answer 'what talked to what yesterday' from its logs.

pages.title: Add Suricata and tune the noise
pages.outcome: Can run Suricata with a correct HOME_NET, trigger a test alert, and tune away the first noisy rule.

pages.title: Sensors compared, and what your lab records
pages.outcome: Can look up which sensor fits a goal and how long each kind of lab log should be kept.

pages.title: What a decoy is, and how one goes wrong
pages.outcome: Can explain why any touch on a decoy is a signal, and list the containment gates a decoy must pass before it runs.

pages.title: Run one contained decoy
pages.outcome: Can start one decoy inside the contained zone, touch it themselves, and decide what a real touch means.

excluded.what: Exposing a decoy or sensor to the internet
excluded.why: Needs every page before it plus operating experience. Out of scope for a first lab.

excluded.what: Testing devices or traffic you do not own
excluded.why: Out of scope by consent, not by size.
Changes the lab from observing to enforcing, with outage risk. A later series if wanted.
